This petition filed by the petitioner/accused No.4. under section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashign the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.30625/2021 in respect of Crime No.182/2022 charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 418, 420, 468, 120(B) read with section 34 of IPC.
2. Heard the argument of learned counsel for petitioner.
Issuing notice to respondent Nos.2 is dispensed with.

3. The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of respondent No.2, the police registered the FIR where he has alleged to be resident of Telangana and he came in contact with one of the accused through mobile, namely Raju in December 2019, while doing business and social work.

Subsequently, the said Raju told that he is having some business at Gulf country and he is having some account in the name of one Senthil and in order to get the said amounts from Gulf Country, he needed some advance amount to pay taxes and some deposits should be shown in the account as per the RBI norms and asked the complainant to deposit same.
Accordingly, the complainant said to have deposited Rs.50,000/- amount in the account of one Senthil-accused No.2.

Subsequently, they asked him to come and to pay Rs.5 lakhs towards the tax and accordingly he came and paid Rs.5 lakhs and said to have complied the RBI rules and the said amount was received by the accused persons.
Thereafter, in total the accused persons have cheated Rs.6.5 lakhs, therefore prayed for taking action.

4. During the investigation, the police arrested the accused persons and came to know the accused persons cheated the complainant and police have recovered more than Rs.3 lakhs and other documents and have filed charge sheet against 7 accused persons and accused No.7 is still absconding.
This petitioner and the accused No.4 challenged the criminal proceedings.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended there is no overt act against this petitioner and there is no allegation against him except that he came along with other accused in the car belonging to some other accused persons and there is no recovery from this petitioner.
Therefore, conducting trial against petitioner is nothing but abuse of process of law.

Therefore, prayed for quashing the Shri Sanjay B Balasundaram @ Sanjay vs State Of Karnataka on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188976498/
2 proceedings.

sentences.text: Per contra learned HCGP objected the petitioner.

Having heard the arguments of both the parties and perusal of the records, it reveals that the petitioner came along with other accused person in the car where the car bearing No.TN70L2106 and in the said car accused Nos.1, 2 and 5 came and met the complainant.
Thereafter, they used same car for the purpose of cheating the complainant stating that the accused persons are having Rs.500 crores to be paid as they have got Rs.6000 crores in the Arab country.
Believing the version, the complainant paid amount through online to accused No.2.

Thereafter, after 20 days once against this petitioner came along with other accused and the other accused received Rs.5 lakhs and Rs.50,000/- by online transfer, totally Rs.6.50 lakhs has been cheated by the accused persons.
Ofcourse there is no recovery from this petitioner, but there is conspiracy with this petitioner along with other accused, they cheated the complainant.
Therefore, it cannot be required, any specific overt act against this petitioner as he has stayed along with co accused in a car.

bearing No.TN70L2106.
7.

Investigation is completed, charge sheet has been filed, there are sufficient materials placed on record for framing the charge sheet against the accused along with the co-accused person for having cheated the complainant.
Such being the case, the petition is devoid of merits and it is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.
